messages:
Rina Kobayashi: We need to settle what “success” means for the FP8/INT8 sprint report + canary gating. Right now everyone is optimizing different things (TTFT vs TPOT vs tokens/sec). Can we align on primary metrics + how we show tradeoffs?

Noah Patel: +1. Also we should explicitly separate prefill vs decode. Otherwise a change that helps decode but hurts prefill looks “flat” end-to-end.

Sofia Ivanova: For hosted traffic, user pain is mostly (1) TTFT for streaming chat (initial token feels slow) and (2) tail latency under mixed prompts. Throughput matters but as a cost lever, not a UX lever.

Hiro Tanaka: Kernel team POV: microbench cares about tokens/sec and achieved FLOPs. But I agree the report needs to be anchored in E2E metrics. TTFT/TPOT are the ones the app teams understand.

Grace Kim: Can we define a single “score” for go/no-go? Or are we comfortable shipping a change that improves TPOT but regresses TTFT a bit?

Marcus Reed: If we do a single score, we’ll fight about weights forever :grimacing:. I’d rather define pass/fail guardrails + then report a Pareto frontier.

Rina Kobayashi: Agree. Proposal: have (A) primary UX metrics, (B) efficiency metrics, (C) safety/quality.

Rina Kobayashi: Draft:
- UX:
  - TTFT p50 + p95 (streaming scenario)
  - TPOT p50 + p95 (decode tokens only, streaming)
  - End-to-end latency p95 (non-streaming completion) for a couple workloads
- Efficiency:
  - tokens/sec (aggregate, steady-state) OR cost proxy (tokens/sec/GPU)
  - GPU utilization (optional)
- Stability:
  - run-to-run variance (cv)

Noah Patel: Small tweak: “tokens/sec” is ambiguous w/ mixed prompt lengths. For decode we should report decode tok/s at fixed output length, and for prefill we should report prefill tok/s at fixed input length. Otherwise scheduling changes muddy it.

Sofia Ivanova: Also queueing matters. We should report queue wait separately when we can (scheduler instrumentation PR is in flight). Tail latency is often queue, not kernel.

Julian Moore: Yep. Once the histograms land we can add:
- queue_wait_ms p95 (prefill, decode)
- service_ms p95 (prefill, decode)

Allison Grant: From dashboard POV: keep it to a small set of top-line panels:
- TTFT p50/p95
- TPOT p50/p95
- tokens/sec (decode)
- requests/sec at fixed SLO (maybe later)
Then let people drill down by model, GPU, quant_mode, kernel_id.

Sean Gallagher: Perf lab variability note: p99 is super noisy. For gating, p95 is safer unless you have a lot of samples. We can still *report* p99 in the sprint report but not block on it.

Connor O'Brien: Release gating: I need a crisp rule. Like “block if TTFT p95 regresses > X% on any gold scenario” etc. If it’s too complex we’ll just end up allowlisting everything.

Jonas Weber: Don’t forget correctness/quality. FP8/INT8 can be “fast” but drift. For this sprint we can treat quality as a hard constraint: drift checks must pass; otherwise not success regardless of perf.

Priyanka Bose: For quality guardrails, we’re using numerical drift vs FP16 baseline on the prompt set. We can define:
- mean abs diff threshold
- max abs diff threshold
- plus a small “semantic” smoke eval on sensitive prompts
But for the success definition, I’d keep it: “no new failures vs baseline”.

Grace Kim: Back to weights: what’s the ordering? If TTFT improves 2% but TPOT regresses 6%, is that a win? That’s where we need guidance.

Noah Patel: IMO for streaming chat:
- TTFT is the top-line
- TPOT is second
But TPOT regression > ~5% is noticeable on long outputs. So we should treat regressions differently by magnitude.

Sofia Ivanova: +1 and depends on workload type:
- Prefill-heavy (long prompts): TTFT dominates
- Decode-heavy (short prompt, long output): TPOT dominates
So success should be “non-regression on both across representative workloads” not a single average.

Marcus Reed: Suggest we define 3 “gold” scenarios and require non-regression on each:
1) Long-context prefill-heavy chat (TTFT focus)
2) Standard chat balanced (TTFT+TPOT)
3) Decode-heavy completion (TPOT+throughput)
Then report the full matrix for everything else.

Rina Kobayashi: This maps to our workload presets already (we can pick one from Llama-family, Qwen-family, Mistral-family). We just need to pick consistent prompt len + output len.

Allison Grant: If you do that, please standardize the tags so the dashboard can have a “gold_scenario=true” filter. Otherwise people won’t find it.

Sean Gallagher: Also pin concurrency for gold scenarios. Throughput changes with concurrency. For TTFT, keep concurrency realistic (like 8/16) not 1.

Hiro Tanaka: Kernel microbench results still matter for “why” and for tuning. But for success criteria I’m ok with E2E metrics as long as we still include microbench tables in the appendix.

Connor O'Brien: Can someone propose actual gating thresholds?

Rina Kobayashi: Strawman gating (nightly canary):
- Hard block:
  - TTFT p95 regression > 3% on any gold scenario
  - TPOT p95 regression > 5% on any gold scenario
  - drift check fails OR kernel auto-select mismatch vs expected
- Soft signal (warn only):
  - tokens/sec regression > 3%
  - queue_wait p95 regression > 10% (since scheduler noise)

Noah Patel: +1. I’d add: if TTFT improves but TPOT regresses, it’s not “block” unless it crosses threshold. Then report the tradeoff explicitly.

Sofia Ivanova: Re: thresholds, make sure it’s “regression vs baseline within same week / same env pin” with robust stats. Otherwise we’ll chase lab jitter.

Sean Gallagher: Yup. Use median-of-5 runs (or trimmed mean) and require effect size > noise floor. Can we set a minimum absolute delta too? Like ignore <1ms TTFT.

Marcus Reed: For TTFT we can set both:
- relative threshold (3%)
- absolute threshold (e.g., 5ms)
Take whichever is larger.

Connor O'Brien: Works for me. I can write that into the perf-canary policy doc.

Allison Grant: For the sprint report, suggest a standard “tradeoff table” per GPU/model:
- baseline vs optimized: TTFT p50/p95, TPOT p50/p95, decode tok/s
- highlight cells with >+/-3% change
Then a short paragraph interpreting why (kernel_id change, batch cap, etc).

Julian Moore: Once we have kernel-selection spans, we can annotate the report: “FP8 attention kernel v2 selected for shapes X/Y, explains TTFT delta”. That helps a lot.

Grace Kim: So what do we call “success” in the exec readout? (Mateo will ask for one sentence.)

Noah Patel: “No regressions on user-visible latency (TTFT/TPOT p95) on gold scenarios, with measurable efficiency gain (tokens/sec) on at least 2/3 model families.”

Rina Kobayashi: Nice. I’ll capture:
1) Primary success metrics = TTFT p95 + TPOT p95 (gold scenarios)
2) Secondary = tokens/sec (decode) / cost proxy
3) Quality = hard constraint (no new drift failures)
4) Report = show tradeoffs, no single composite score

Connor O'Brien: :thumbsup: Please also drop this into the ADR draft so we stop re-litigating.

Rina Kobayashi: Will do. I’ll update the benchmark methodology + canary thresholds doc today and link here.

Allison Grant: When you have final metric names/tags, send them to me so dashboard panels match exactly.

Sean Gallagher: And ping me before enabling “block” mode; I want at least 3 nights of stability first.

Rina Kobayashi: Deal.
